fields.AN_Notes: Pre-post evaluation of a 7-hour AI literacy course on machine learning concepts with university students in Hong Kong; research question 3 asks whether the course narrows gaps between genders and study backgrounds. Bias_Axes Gender because female and male participants are compared on concepts test, literacy and empowerment (Sections 4.1, 4.4, Table 5); study background and programming experience are non-social variables and not coded. Harm_Types None: the work establishes no harm mechanism of an AI system; gender stereotypes are cited to explain the empowerment gap. Mitigation: the course is an identifiable training intervention whose reported result is that the pre-course gender gap in self-perceived AI empowerment no longer existed after the course (Table 5); it addresses a gender gap in AI learning, not algorithmic bias, so Organisational_Process and Evaluated are limited to this training and its own pre-post result. AN_Task None: AI is the learning content, the work describes no professional task performed with AI. Gender is used as two categories (both genders) without definition. Theory_Reference No: self-efficacy (Bandura) and programming empowerment frame empowerment, not gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: UNESCO and IRCAI issue brief with own prompt-based studies on GPT-2, ChatGPT, Llama 2 and Ada-002 embeddings: word-embedding association test, regard of sentence completions, diversity of completions by culture and gender, and story generation by gender and nationality. Prompts are the research instrument; sentence-completion and story prompts carry no codable technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from Study 1 (gender and career or family, age and pleasantness), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from Study 2 (subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North and South). Intersectional because Study 3 reports occupations that depend on the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard), although the work lists the need for intersectional analysis as a limitation. Harm_Types from own results: Stereotyping (gendered role associations, stereotyped occupations and story themes) and Derogatory_Language (sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions). Repetitive output for women and local groups is a difference in output diversity and style and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Mitigation recommendations only: diverse and inclusive training data and data augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF guidelines (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments, diverse teams, stakeholder participation and literacy initiatives (Organisational_Process). The RLHF observation in Study 2 is a cross-model comparison, not an evaluation of an isolated mitigation, so status Proposed. Gender is analysed as woman and man, girl and boy; the statement on the complexity of human gender identities is a recommendation the analysis does not follow. Bias is defined explicitly as algorithmic bias that unfairly discriminates. Theory_Reference No: the implicit association test is a measurement method, no theory frames gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Short conceptual risk analysis of ChatGPT and AI in social work (data security, algorithmic bias, ethics, legal risks) with countermeasures. Bias_Axes Socioeconomic: economically disadvantaged groups are the work's own example of data imbalance in social services; 'minority groups' and 'marginalized groups' stay unspecified and are not coded. Harm_Types from the work's own risk argument: Disparate_Performance (inadequate data on underrepresented groups hinders systems from accurately gauging their needs) and Direct_Discrimination (feedback-loop bias leading to denial of services and resources 'based on their inherent characteristics'); the work does not itself separate direct from indirect discrimination, and the phrase is read as a decision changing with the group attribute. The single sentence that biases threaten to perpetuate stereotypes is asserted without mechanism and not coded as Stereotyping. Mitigation proposed: diverse and representative datasets (Pre_Processing); transparency, explainability, oversight, training of social workers and legal regulation (Organisational_Process). Training ChatGPT to warn on sensitive topics concerns illicit content, not bias, and is not coded as In_Training. AN_Task Case_Assessment_Decision_Support for risk assessment algorithms and AI-driven decisions about services. Bias is explained through data imbalance and feedback loops without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual, literature-based paper on AI (machine learning, intelligent tutoring, teacherbots, VR simulation, AI grading) in higher education and its implications for social work education. Bias_Axes None: 'AI algorithms may reinforce racial and gender stereotypes' is cited from Howard and Borenstein (2017) and not developed as the work's own example (codebook boundary anchor VSZM7CT6, a record of this work). Harm_Types None: developer bias in child-protection predictive risk modelling and the beneficence problem are reported from cited work, not established by the work's own argument. Mitigation None: the proposed critical digital literacies address AI understanding in social work education generally and are not presented as a measure against bias. AN_Task Teaching_Further_Education for AI in teaching, assessment, tutoring and simulation in social work education. Gender is no object; 'gender stereotypes' appears once in a cited sentence. Bias is understood as structural inequity built into human-made systems without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only. Theory_Reference Yes: Braidotti's critical posthumanism, whose 'Convergence' of speedy transformations and persistent inequalities directly precedes and frames the work's statement on bias and structural inequity, and frames its questions of power; the line between a framing concept and an illustrative mention is a recorded open question of the codebook. Feministisch stays nein because Braidotti is used as posthuman theory without a gender-related power analysis.

Bias_Ungleichheit.snippet: AI systems are created by humans, like conventional human systems, bias and structural inequity can be built into them, even if inadvertently.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual, literature-based paper on AI (machine learning, intelligent tutoring, teacherbots, VR simulation, AI grading) in higher education and its implications for social work education. Bias_Axes None: 'AI algorithms may reinforce racial and gender stereotypes' is cited from Howard and Borenstein (2017) and not developed as the work's own example (codebook boundary anchor VSZM7CT6, a record of this work). Harm_Types None: developer bias in child-protection predictive risk modelling and the beneficence problem are reported from cited work, not established by the work's own argument. Mitigation None: the proposed critical digital literacies address AI understanding in social work education generally and are not presented as a measure against bias. AN_Task Teaching_Further_Education for AI in teaching, assessment, tutoring and simulation in social work education. Gender is no object; 'gender stereotypes' appears once in a cited sentence. Bias is understood as structural inequity built into human-made systems without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only. Theory_Reference Yes: Braidotti's critical posthumanism, whose 'Convergence' of speedy transformations and persistent inequalities directly precedes and frames the work's statement on bias and structural inequity, and frames its questions of power; the line between a framing concept and an illustrative mention is a recorded open question of the codebook. Feministisch stays nein because Braidotti is used as posthuman theory without a gender-related power analysis.
